Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace

分类方向评测与可靠性 / 评测体系主题evaluation / benchmarks
Yijun Pan, Yukun Lian, Kunyu Shi, Junbo Li, Hongwei Xue, Sicong Xie et al.
high · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 这项基准把代理评测从短程任务扩展到跨境经营中的长期决策，迫使模型处理不完全信息、资本投入、延迟回报、市场变化和合规约束。对研究端到端代理、长期推理与可靠评测的人来说，它还提供了利润、技能指标、动作归因和机制消融，能区分真正的经营能力与模拟器捷径；十五个前沿模型的最终净资产均值相差九倍，且最佳模型仍落后于人工策略。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 16）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有代理基准很少评估代理在长期商业运营中的机会判断、资本决策、适应能力和合规行为。

02
方法

构建一个让代理向供应商采购并向买家销售的跨境商店环境，并结合真实采购数据与校准后的市场条件。

03
差异

它用长期耦合且延迟的商业后果作为核心测试，同时以利润、技能指标、人工策略对照和动作归因解释成败。

04
证据

论文评估十五个前沿模型，报告最终净资产均值相差九倍、最佳模型落后于人工策略，并通过机制消融检验模拟器捷径。

摘要

经营企业要求智能系统从不完整信号中发现机会，在不确定性下投入资本，适应不断变化市场中的延迟结果，并在合法交易前满足监管要求。论文提出商业竞技场：让人工智能代理在基于真实阿里巴巴采购数据和权威来源校准的市场环境中，长期经营一家跨境商店，通过利润、技能指标、人工策略对照、动作级收益归因和机制消融评估其能力。对十五个前沿模型的评测显示，其最终净资产均值相差九倍，而表现最好的模型仍落后于人工设计策略，说明商业运营对语言模型代理仍然困难。

DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?

分类方向评测与可靠性 / 评测体系主题evaluation / benchmarks
Mizanur Rahman, Mohammed Saidul Islam, Ridwan Mahbub, Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque Prince
high · 2026-08-11

为什么值得看 它把数据科学代理的评测从代码生成推进到真实计算机环境中的长程执行，能帮助研究者定位工具编排、操作系统落地和多步推理的具体瓶颈；对开发可验证代理策略和训练数据尤其有用。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 7）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有基准缺少真实计算机交互，无法检验代理是否能完成端到端的数据科学流程。

02
方法

基准包含275项覆盖数据科学全生命周期的任务，每项任务都要求依据中间输出决策并协调多个工具。

03
差异

评估器不仅检查代码执行，还确定性验证分析结果、可视化输出和模型性能。

04
证据

在15个闭源和开源模型上，最强模型成功率为56.70%，所有开源代理成功率均低于1%。

摘要

现实数据科学工作流横跨数据整理、探索、建模、可视化和验证，并要求代理在真实操作环境中协调使用笔记本、集成开发环境、终端、浏览器和数据库。本文发布数据科学代理基准，包含覆盖完整生命周期的275项任务，并通过确定性评估器检查分析正确性、视觉输出和模型性能；对15个闭源及开源模型的实验显示，最强代理克劳德四点六索奈特的任务成功率仅为56.70%，所有开源代理均低于1%，主要失败于工具编排、操作系统落地和多步推理。

Xiaohongshu Inc
high · 2026-08-11

为什么值得看 它把智能体评测从短指令问答推进到多周、持续变化的生活环境，能检验模型是否会主动检查世界、管理时机、维护长期计划并遵守未明说的约束；这对个人助理和长期任务智能体尤其关键。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 15）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有基准缺少对智能体在多周动态生活任务中的主动性、持续性和长期一致性的测量。

02
方法

作者构建二百个跨十个日常领域的脚本化多周任务，并在包含二十二个模拟服务的自主推进世界中运行。

03
差异

环境变化不会全部主动通知智能体，评分只读取其实际留下的结果，并同时检查终态、行动时机和隐含约束。

04
证据

七个当前模型均取得较低分数，作者还计划开源任务、环境和评测框架。

摘要

现有大语言模型智能体评测大多使用静态环境中的短期、封闭请求，无法反映现实生活中持续数周、环境自行变化且约束常未明说的任务。本文介绍一个包含十个日常生活领域、二百个长期任务的基准：任务运行于由二十二个模拟服务构成的世界，环境按自身时钟推进，评测依据智能体留下的实际结果，细致检查最终状态、行动时效性和隐含约束遵守情况；对七个当前领先模型的评测均显示得分较低。

360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents

分类方向评测与可靠性 / 评测体系主题evaluation / benchmarks
Kenta Watanabe, Atsuyuki Miyai, Mizuki Takenawa, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Toshihiko Yamasaki
high · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 该基准把城市级具身导航评测推进到更接近真实街区的光写实环境，并用定位、地标搜索、路径规划和空间关系推理检验智能体能力；最强受测模型仅获百分之十七点一的成绩，而人类为百分之七十七点三，说明现有多模态智能体在复杂城市探索上仍有明显推理缺口。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 9）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有室外导航基准在光写实程度或场景复杂度上不足，难以反映真实城市环境中的探索要求。

02
方法

研究者从六百零二段全景视频重建东京秋叶原街区，并制作覆盖三类能力的一百七十五项任务。

03
差异

该基准将光写实街区、城市级路径推理和空间关系推理结合到同一评测环境中。

04
证据

人类得分为百分之七十七点三，表现最强的模型得分为百分之十七点一。

摘要

本文提出一个用于评估具身智能体城市探索能力的基准，环境由全景视频构建而成，具有光写实特征。该基准基于日本东京秋叶原街区的现实重建，使用覆盖八十五条街道的六百零二段全景视频，并包含一百七十五个人工设计任务，分为环境理解、路径推理和空间推理三类，涵盖定位、地标搜索、路径规划及空间关系推理等能力。对基于大语言多模态模型的智能体进行评测发现，即使表现最强的模型，其成绩也远低于人类，显示城市尺度的具身导航与推理仍面临重大挑战。

Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds

分类方向模型与训练方法 / 架构设计主题diffusion / generative modeling
Zihao Liu, Xiaolong Shen, Zhenglin Zhou, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang
high · 2026-08-11

为什么值得看 这项工作把共享变分自编码器的视频模型最终去噪潜变量变成可复用的四维生成接口，绕过先生成红绿蓝视频、再重建四维场景的级联流程。单个检查点可直接迁移到同一变分自编码器家族的多个视频扩散变换器上，并在两个基准上以投影基于迪诺的第一分数超过匹配级联方法，适合关注动态几何、跨视频生成器迁移和训练成本的研究者。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 108）
方法解读
01
问题

现有四维生成要么先重建红绿蓝视频再生成四维场景，容易产生分布偏移和误差传播，要么绑定特定视频生成器。

02
方法

方法将视频最终去噪潜变量对齐到预训练四维解码器的标记网格，并用逐帧及全局时空注意力细化四维预测。

03
差异

它绕过红绿蓝中间结果，并把四维预测与共享变分自编码器下的多个视频扩散变换器解耦。

04
证据

在文本四维二百和图像四维二百基准上，投影基于迪诺的第一分数分别超过匹配级联方法二点八八至三点四五分和五点八一分，且人工评价更偏好其几何、时间稳定性和总体质量。

摘要

四维生成旨在根据文本或图像等条件合成动态三维场景。论文利用共享变分自编码器的视频模型最终去噪潜变量，提出直接从潜变量生成四维场景的方法，并将其实现为潜变量到四维模型：该方法绕过红绿蓝视频，将视频潜变量与预训练四维解码器的标记网格对齐，再通过逐帧和全局时空注意力进行细化；使用约一千个重建视频片段训练的单个检查点，可在同一变分自编码器家族的多个视频扩散变换器之间保持不变地迁移，并在两个基准上超过匹配的同潜变量级联方法。

high · 2026-08-11

为什么值得看 这项工作直接针对生成器后训练中的弗雷歇指标投机问题：模型可能只改善固定特征空间中的分数，却损害视觉质量或其他特征空间中的分布对齐。通过让特征表示对抗性地适应真实分布与生成分布之间的差异，并用真实特征白化稳定极小极大优化，它为一步生成器后训练提供了比固定预训练特征更有适应性的分布级目标。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 23）
方法解读
01
问题

固定的预训练特征空间无法完整反映真实样本分布与生成样本分布之间的差异。

02
方法

方法加入一个对抗性学习的表示，使其最大化弗雷歇差异而生成器在该表示中最小化同一差异，并对白化后的真实特征进行尺度与协方差归一化。

03
差异

相较于仅使用静态特征的弗雷歇损失，它把分布距离的特征空间变成可适应且受白化约束的表示。

04
证据

大量实验显示，该方法在两类生成骨干网络和不同模型规模上都能改善一步生成器后训练。

摘要

弗雷歇距离近期成为生成器后训练中的有效分布级目标，可补充传统的样本级扩散损失和流匹配损失，但直接优化弗雷歇目标可能导致弗雷歇投机：目标指标持续改善，而视觉质量以及其他特征空间中的分布对齐停滞或恶化。该方法在原有静态弗雷歇目标上加入可学习的对抗表示，并通过真实特征白化限制特征放大；实验表明，它在不同规模的两类生成骨干网络上都能持续改善一步生成器后训练效果。

high · 2026-08-12

为什么值得看 这项工作把视频去反射中的三个瓶颈连成闭环：用物理约束合成成对视频数据，用视频扩散先验进行单步清除，并提供专门基准。对需要处理玻璃拍摄视频的视觉系统而言，它同时缓解了训练数据不足、时间一致性和评测缺失问题；摘要还称其推理速度快于非扩散基线。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 3）
方法解读
01
问题

视频反射去除缺少真实成对数据、时间一致的模型和专用基准。

02
方法

方法先模拟粗糙度导致的模糊、厚度导致的重影和反射率变化，再用视频扩散先验结合潜变量适配与单步像素几何细化恢复透射内容。

03
差异

它将物理约束的视频合成、扩散式去反射和评测基准统一在一个闭环中，而不是只处理单张图像。

04
证据

摘要报告该方法在自建基准和多个公开图像基准上取得领先性能，并比非扩散基线推理更快。

摘要

玻璃拍摄的视频常含有会降低画质并干扰下游视觉任务的反射，但视频去反射因缺少成对视频数据、时间一致的去除模型和专用评测基准而研究不足。该工作构建了一个闭环系统：在结构空间中进行物理约束增强并通过视频扩散渲染器生成成对数据，利用反射感知的潜变量适配和单步像素几何细化实现基于扩散的视频去反射，同时建立支持全参考评测和真实世界人工感知评测的基准；实验声称在该基准和多个公开图像基准上取得领先性能，并且推理速度快于非扩散基线。

high · 2026-08-11

为什么值得看 这项工作把视觉分辨率变成推理时可分配的计算资源：模型先低分辨率浏览长文档，再按需放大局部区域，并通过监督微调与强化学习学习放大轨迹。对长文档视觉问答而言，它在不依赖外部检索器的情况下声称同时提升准确率、降低幻觉和推理延迟，适合关注视觉语言模型推理效率与长上下文退化的研究者。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 10）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

长文档中的多页面视觉推理会带来较高推理成本和上下文退化。

02
方法

模型先以低分辨率处理文档，再通过区域级放大轨迹进行监督微调和强化学习训练。

03
差异

该方法在模型内部自适应选择需要高分辨率观察的区域，而不是始终以高分辨率处理整份文档或依赖外部检索。

04
证据

八十亿参数模型在文档视觉问答基准上较基线提升四点三至十六点四个准确率百分点，并声称长文档幻觉降低超过百分之四十、推理延迟降低百分之四十一至百分之六十八。

摘要

长文档理解需要在大量视觉信息丰富的页面之间进行推理，因此推理成本高且容易出现上下文退化。该工作提出一种智能体式视觉感知框架，将视觉分辨率视为可自适应分配的推理时资源：模型从低分辨率开始，仅对需要更细证据的区域选择性放大，且不依赖外部检索器；作者构建了包含一百七十九万？

为什么值得看 这项工作把电影视频压缩为可查询、可编辑的知识图和多媒体资产层，而不是只学习难以解释的连续潜表示；如果其重建驱动的文本反馈确实有效，视频生成智能体就能直接操作镜头、状态和素材关系，并在测试时细化表示。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers
方法解读
01
问题

高质量电影缺少同时支持内容保真、智能体推理和视频编辑的结构化表示。

02
方法

方法把视频编码为包含层级节点、状态节点和链接资产的知识图，再根据视频重建差异生成自然语言更新方向。

03
差异

它用文本描述和类型化关系连接图像、音频与视频资产，并支持外循环策略伪训练和可选的测试时表示细化。

Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace

CategoryAreaEvaluation and Reliability / Evaluation SystemsTopicevaluation / benchmarks
Yijun Pan, Yukun Lian, Kunyu Shi, Junbo Li, Hongwei Xue, Sicong Xie et al.
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This benchmark moves agent evaluation from short-horizon tasks to long-run cross-border operations with partial information, capital commitments, delayed rewards, market shifts, and regulatory constraints. It is useful for researchers studying end-to-end agents, long-horizon reasoning, and trustworthy evaluation because it combines profit with skill metrics, action attribution, human-designed baselines, and mechanism ablations; across 15 frontier models, mean final net worth differs ninefold, and the best model still trails human strategies.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 16)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing agent benchmarks rarely test opportunity discovery, capital allocation, adaptation, and compliance in sustained business operations.

02
Method

The paper builds a cross-border shop environment in which an agent buys from suppliers and sells to buyers using real sourcing data and calibrated market conditions.

03
Difference

It evaluates long-horizon coupled consequences while adding profit analysis, skill-level diagnostics, human-designed strategies, and action-level attribution.

04
Evidence

Evaluation covers 15 frontier models, finds a ninefold gap in mean final net worth, shows the best model behind human strategies, and uses mechanism ablations to test for simulator shortcuts.

Abstract

Running a business is a challenging form of intelligent work. Operators must infer opportunities from partial signals, commit capital under uncertainty, adapt to delayed outcomes in a changing market, and satisfy regulatory obligations before trading legally. Frontier LLM agents can increasingly complete complex workflows, yet business-related capabilities are rarely evaluated in existing agent benchmarks. We introduce Business Arena, a controlled environment where an AI agent runs a cross-border shop, buying from suppliers and selling to buyers over a long horizon. We ground the arena in real Alibaba.com sourcing data and market conditions calibrated from authoritative sources. Delayed and coupled consequences make individual business decisions difficult to judge, but their combined outcome is measurable through profit. Because profit alone cannot explain why an agent succeeds or fails, we compare agents with human-designed strategies to estimate available opportunity, use skill-level metrics to reveal underlying strengths and weaknesses, and trace realized gains and losses to the actions that produced them. We use mechanism ablations to establish that strong results reflect genuine business intelligence rather than neglect or simulator-specific shortcuts. We evaluate 15 frontier models and find a ninefold difference in mean final net worth. Even the best model falls behind human-designed strategies, indicating that business operation remains challenging for LLM agents. Skill-level analysis reveals operating styles, from margin-focused premium sellers to high-turnover wholesalers and customer-service specialists, while action-level attribution identifies the sourcing, pricing, and recovery decisions that create or destroy value. Together, Business Arena takes a first step toward a realistic and trustworthy testbed for evaluating end-to-end business agents.

DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?

CategoryAreaEvaluation and Reliability / Evaluation SystemsTopicevaluation / benchmarks
Mizanur Rahman, Mohammed Saidul Islam, Ridwan Mahbub, Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque Prince
high · 2026-08-11

Why it matters It moves data-science agent evaluation beyond code generation to long-horizon execution in real computer environments, giving algorithm researchers a way to isolate failures in tool orchestration, OS grounding, and multi-step reasoning. This is especially useful for developing trainable and verifiable agent policies.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 7)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing benchmarks lack real-computer interaction and cannot test complete end-to-end data-science workflows.

02
Method

The benchmark provides 275 tasks spanning the full data-science lifecycle, with intermediate-output grounding and coordinated use of multiple tools.

03
Difference

Its deterministic evaluator checks analytical correctness, visual outputs, and model performance rather than code execution alone.

04
Evidence

Across 15 closed- and open-source models, the strongest model reaches 56.70% task success while every open-source agent remains below 1%.

Abstract

Real-world data science involves long-horizon workflows that span data wrangling, exploration, modeling, visualization, and validation, and require coordinated use of tools such as notebooks, IDEs, terminals, browsers, and databases within real operating environments. Yet existing benchmarks lack real-computer interaction and do not evaluate whether agents can execute complete end-to-end data-science workflows in realistic computing environments, failing to capture the multi-stage, multi-tool nature of data-science practice. We introduce DSAgentBench, the first benchmark to evaluate whether agents can automate full data-science workflows inside real computer environments. DSAgentBench contains 275 diverse tasks covering the entire data-science life-cycle, reflecting the complexity and tool coordination required in practice. Each task requires grounding decisions in intermediate outputs and coordinated tool use, and includes a deterministic evaluator that verifies analytical correctness, visual outputs, and model performance rather than code-only execution. Our extensive experiments with 15 closed- and open-source models show that even the strongest agent, Claude-4.6-Sonnet, achieves only 56.70% task success, while all open-source agents remain below 1%, frequently failing at tool orchestration, OS grounding, and multi-step reasoning. These results reveal a substantial capability gap between current agentic systems and real data-science workflows, positioning DSAgentBench as a foundation for developing grounded, verifiable, autonomous data-science agents. We release DSAgentBench at https://github.com/vis-nlp/DSAgentBench.

VibeLifeBench: Can Your Life Agent Be Proactive and Persistent in a Living World?

CategoryAreaEvaluation and Reliability / Evaluation SystemsTopicevaluation / benchmarks
Xiaohongshu Inc
high · 2026-08-11

Why it matters It moves agent evaluation beyond short, static requests to multi-week life tasks with silent world changes, testing whether a system can inspect proactively, choose when to act or ask, preserve a coherent plan, and respect unstated constraints. This is directly useful for personal assistants and other long-running agents.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 15)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing benchmarks do not measure proactive and persistent behavior over multi-week tasks in a changing environment.

02
Method

The benchmark contains 200 scripted tasks across ten everyday domains in a simulated world with 22 mock services and an autonomous clock.

03
Difference

Some world changes are silent, and grading reads only the agent's persistent outputs while checking end state, action timeliness, and implicit constraints.

04
Evidence

Seven evaluated models all score low, and the authors plan to release the tasks, environments, and evaluation framework.

Abstract

Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed as personal assistants. Existing evaluations, however, mostly use short, self-contained requests in static environments. Everyday life assistance is different. A task runs for weeks rather than minutes. The world keeps changing while the agent is not being prompted. Many constraints are never stated outright. An agent that merely answers the request in front of it will fail at such a task. What is needed instead is an agent that stays proactive and consistent. It decides on its own when to act, when to ask, and when to stay silent. It notices changes that nobody announced. It keeps one plan coherent from the first day to the last. No current benchmark measures this. We introduce VibeLifeBench, a benchmark of 200 long-horizon tasks across ten everyday-life domains. Each task is a scripted multi-week timeline in a simulated world of 22 mock services. The world advances on its own clock, and many of its changes are silent, so only an agent that re-inspects the world discovers them. Every task is graded by fine-grained, weighted checks that read only what the agent actually left behind, covering the end state, the timeliness of its actions, and whether it upheld the implicit constraints. We evaluate seven frontier models. All of them score low, which shows how far current agents are from assisting with real life. We will open-source all tasks, environments, and the evaluation framework.

360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents

CategoryAreaEvaluation and Reliability / Evaluation SystemsTopicevaluation / benchmarks
Kenta Watanabe, Atsuyuki Miyai, Mizuki Takenawa, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Toshihiko Yamasaki
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This benchmark moves embodied-navigation evaluation toward a more realistic urban-district setting and tests localization, landmark search, path planning, and spatial reasoning together; the best evaluated model scores only 17.1% versus 77.3% for humans, exposing a large reasoning gap for multimodal agents in complex city exploration.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 9)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing outdoor navigation benchmarks lack enough photorealism or scene complexity to represent real urban exploration.

02
Method

The authors reconstruct Tokyo’s Akihabara district from 602 360-degree video segments and create 175 tasks across three capability categories.

03
Difference

The benchmark combines photorealistic district navigation with path reasoning and relational spatial reasoning in one evaluation environment.

04
Evidence

Humans achieve 77.3%, while the strongest evaluated model, Gemini 2.5 Flash, achieves 17.1%.

Abstract

We present 360CityArena, a benchmark for evaluating the urban exploration capabilities of embodied agents within a photorealistic environment constructed from 360-degree videos. Existing outdoor benchmarks either lack sufficient photorealism or complexity, resulting in a considerable gap from real-world urban environments. 360CityArena is built on a realistic reconstruction of the Akihabara district in Tokyo, Japan, using 602 360-degree video segments covering 85 streets, and consists of 175 meticulously human-crafted tasks. It encompasses three task categories: Environment Understanding, Path Reasoning, and Spatial Reasoning, covering fundamental abilities required for urban exploration, such as localization, landmark search, path planning, and relational spatial reasoning, thereby enabling comprehensive evaluation in realistic urban scenes. Our evaluation using state-of-the-art LMM-based agents shows that even the strongest model, Gemini 2.5 Flash, performs far below human level (human: 77.3% vs. Gemini 2.5 Flash: 17.1%), revealing substantial challenges that remain in city-scale embodied navigation and reasoning. 360CityArena provides a necessary and challenging testbed for photorealistic urban-district navigation and spatial reasoning.

Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Zihao Liu, Xiaolong Shen, Zhenglin Zhou, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang
high · 2026-08-11

Why it matters The paper turns final denoised latents from video models with a shared VAE into a reusable interface for explicit 4D generation, avoiding the usual RGB-video-to-4D cascade. One checkpoint transfers unchanged across multiple video diffusion transformers in the same VAE family and beats matched cascades on two benchmarks, which matters for researchers targeting dynamic geometry, generator portability, and lower error propagation.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 108)
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing 4D systems either reconstruct generated RGB videos with a separate model, causing distribution mismatch and error propagation, or depend on one video generator.

02
Method

The method aligns a video model's final denoised latent with a pretrained 4D decoder's token grid and refines it using frame-wise and global spatiotemporal attention.

03
Difference

It removes the RGB intermediate and separates 4D prediction from individual video diffusion transformers within a shared VAE family.

04
Evidence

On Text4D-200 and I4D-200, it improves projection-based DINO-F1 over matched same-latent Wan+4RC cascades by 2.88–3.45 and 5.81 points, respectively, with higher human preference for geometry, temporal stability, and overall quality.

Abstract

4D generation synthesizes dynamic 3D scenes from conditions such as text or images. Existing methods either reconstruct generated RGB videos with a separate 4D model or adapt a particular video generator to predict geometry directly. The former suffers from distribution mismatch and error propagation, whereas the latter ties 4D prediction to a specific generator and may require retraining when the generator or conditioning regime changes. We ask whether the final denoised latents of video models that share a variational autoencoder (VAE) can instead provide a reusable interface to explicit 4D prediction. Building on this insight, we introduce direct latent-to-4D generation and instantiate it as Latent-to-4D, which bypasses RGB by aligning a video latent with the token grid of a pretrained 4D decoder and refining it through frame-wise and global spatiotemporal attention. Trained on roughly 1K existing reconstruction clips, a single checkpoint transfers unchanged across multiple video diffusion transformers within the same VAE family. On Text4D-200 and I4D-200, Latent-to-4D surpasses matched same-latent Wan+4RC cascades in projection-based DINO-F1 by 2.88--3.45 and 5.81 points, respectively, while also being preferred by human raters for geometry, temporal stability, and overall quality.

AdvFD: Boosting Visual Generation via Adversarial Fr'echet Distance Loss

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Mingju Gao, Jingkai Zhou, Kun Gai, Changqian Yu, Hao Tang
high · 2026-08-11

Why it matters This paper targets Fréchet-metric hacking in generator post-training, where a model can improve the score in a fixed feature space while visual quality or alignment in other spaces stagnates or worsens. By adapting the feature representation adversarially and stabilizing it with real-feature whitening, AdvFD offers a more responsive distribution-level objective for one-step generator post-training than fixed pretrained features.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 23)
Method brief
01
Problem

Static pretrained feature spaces provide incomplete views of the discrepancy between real and generated distributions.

02
Method

AdvFD adds a learnable representation that maximizes the Fréchet discrepancy against the generator, while real-feature whitening normalizes scale and covariance geometry during the min-max optimization.

03
Difference

Unlike a Fréchet loss built only on fixed features, it learns an adaptive feature space while constraining feature amplification.

04
Evidence

Extensive experiments report consistent gains for one-step generator post-training across JiT and pMF backbones and different model scales.

Abstract

Fréchet distance has recently emerged as an effective distribution-level objective for generator post-training, complementing the conventional sample-level diffusion and flow-matching losses. However, directly optimizing Fréchet objectives can cause Fréchet hacking. The target metrics keep improving, but visual quality and Fréchet alignment in other feature spaces may stagnate or deteriorate. We attribute this failure to the static pretrained feature spaces used by existing Fréchet losses. These feature spaces provide incomplete and fixed views of the differences between real and generated distributions. To address this limitation, we propose Adversarial Fréchet Distance (AdvFD), which complements the static representation targets in FD-Loss with a calibrated adversarially learned representation. AdvFD augments the original static Fréchet objective with a learnable representation that adversarially maximizes the Fréchet discrepancy between real and generated samples, while the generator minimizes the same discrepancy in the resulting adaptive feature space. To prevent the adversarial representation from trivially increasing the objective through feature amplification, we further introduce real-feature whitening, which normalizes its scale and covariance geometry and stabilizes the min--max optimization. Extensive experiments show that AdvFD consistently improves one-step generator post-training across both JiT and pMF backbones and across different model scales.

From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Zepeng Wang, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Yuxuan Chen, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters The work connects the three main bottlenecks in video dereflection: paired-data scarcity, temporal consistency, and missing evaluation protocols. For vision systems processing footage through glass, its physics-grounded synthesis supplies training pairs, while the diffusion model removes reflections in one denoising step; the abstract also reports faster inference than non-diffusion baselines.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 3)
Method brief
01
Problem

Video reflection removal lacks realistic paired videos, temporally coherent models, and dedicated benchmarks.

02
Method

The pipeline simulates glass roughness blur, thickness ghosting, and reflectance variation, then adapts a pretrained video diffusion prior with reflection-aware latent adaptation and one-step pixel-geometric refinement.

03
Difference

It combines physics-grounded video synthesis, diffusion-based removal, and benchmark evaluation in one closed loop instead of focusing on single-image removal.

04

Abstract

Videos captured through glass often contain reflections that degrade visual quality and interfere with downstream vision tasks. Although single-image reflection removal has been extensively studied, video reflection removal remains largely underexplored due to the lack of paired video data, temporally coherent removal models, and dedicated evaluation benchmarks. We present a closed-loop framework that unifies physics-grounded reflection simulation, diffusion-based video dereflection, and benchmark evaluation. Our S2R-Synthesis pipeline generates paired reflected and reflection-free videos by performing physics-grounded augmentation in the structure space and rendering realistic reflected videos with a trained video diffusion renderer; the augmentation models key glass-related effects including roughness-induced blur, thickness-induced ghosting, and reflectance variation. Based on the synthesized data, we introduce S2R-Removal, the first diffusion-based video reflection removal model, which adapts a pretrained video diffusion prior through reflection-aware latent adaptation and one-step pixel-geometric refinement, recovering the clean transmission in a single denoising step. We further build S2R-Bench, the first benchmark for video reflection removal, supporting both full-reference evaluation and real-world human perceptual assessment. Experiments on S2R-Bench and multiple public image benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and faster inference than even non-diffusion baselines, and validate the effectiveness of S2R-Synthesis. Project page: https://codingwzp.github.io/VideoDereflection_S2R.

Method brief
01
Problem

Reasoning across many visually rich document pages is expensive and vulnerable to context rot.

02
Method

The model begins with low-resolution perception and learns region-level zoom trajectories through SFT followed by RL.

03
Difference

It adaptively allocates high-resolution viewing inside the model instead of processing every page at high resolution or using an external retriever.

Abstract

Long-document understanding often requires reasoning over many visually rich pages, making inference costly and prone to context rot. In this work, we propose InSight-doc, an agentic visual perception framework that treats visual resolution as an adaptive reasoning-time resource. InSight-doc starts from low resolution and selectively zooms into high-resolution regions for finer evidence, without relying on any external retriever. To train such an agent, we construct an active-perception corpus of 17.9K high-quality SFT examples with region-level zoom-in trajectories, accompanied by 19.2K hard RL examples. Through SFT+RL, InSight-doc-8B improves the baseline by 4.3--16.4 accuracy points over document VQA benchmarks. On long documents, it reduces hallucination by more than 40% and inference latency by 41%--68% while maintaining an accuracy lead. Our code, datasets, and model are released at https://github.com/m-Just/InSight-doc .

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers
Method brief
01
Problem

High-quality films lack a structured representation that preserves content while supporting agent reasoning and manipulation.

02
Method

The system maps each video to a knowledge graph with hierarchical and state text nodes, linked media assets, and typed relations, then reconstructs the video and uses reconstruction differences as textual update directions.

Abstract

Creative agents still lack an effective way to learn from high-quality human films, limiting their ability to produce cinematic-grade videos. A key challenge is the absence of a structured video representation that is both faithful to film content and directly usable for agentic reasoning and manipulation. To address the challenge, we propose the Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder), a framework for learning agent-native video representations via agentic auto-encoding. AVA-Encoder transforms a video into a knowledge graph (KG) representation and then reconstructs it back into video. Its hierarchy and state nodes store structured text, while a linked asset layer holds generated images, audio, and video. Typed edges preserve the relations between these text descriptions and assets in a form that agents can easily understand, query, and edit. The video reconstruction differences drive a textual-gradient optimization framework, which expresses evaluation feedback as natural-language update directions for Data-Independent Encoding Policy Pseudo-Training in the outer loop and optional Data-Dependent KG Representation Refinement in the test-time inner loop. Extensive experiments show that AVA-Encoder improves by 20.7 percentage points over the strongest external baseline. In the controlled policy-only setting, its pseudo-trained shot-level Agentic Video Encoder policy also outperforms a carefully human-tuned policy while using 74.3% fewer system-prompt tokens. We release the complete AVA-Encoder framework, a reliable agentic video reconstruction benchmark, and the first dataset of high-quality film KG representations.

ComBodied Agents: a New Paradigm of Human-Centric Agentic AI

Qianggang Ding, Xingyao Wang, Rui Feng, Zhibin Wang, Feixiang Wang, Kelong Mao et al.

Why it matters This work shifts agent design from completing external tasks to sustaining a person’s evolving state and agency. Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 174)
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing digital and embodied agents do not reliably infer a person’s underlying state, intent, or appropriate support after an event.

02
Method

The framework closes a loop over event-based perception, longitudinal memory, personal world models, and intervention policies constrained by consent, uncertainty, safety, reversibility, and user control.

Abstract

After an older adult misses a medication dose, a software agent can send another reminder and an embodied agent can bring the medication. Yet neither explains whether the person forgot, is confused, has side effects, or deliberately refused, nor what support is appropriate. 01
Problem

The model targets high expert capacity with bounded per-token compute while keeping very long-context training and diverse capabilities stable.

Method

Abstract

We introduce Motif 3, a decoder-only Mixture-of-Experts language model with 314 billion total parameters and 13.2 billion activated per token. Each sparse MoE layer contains 384 routed experts, with eight selected per token. This fine-grained sparsity provides substantial expert capacity while limiting computation. 为什么值得看 这项工作面向边缘推理系统中检测与细粒度分类串行占用图形处理器的问题，给出了把分类模型迁移到专用神经加速器并与检测器并发执行的完整工程路径。对使用英伟达边缘芯片的实时视觉系统而言，它可在不增加检测器流水线开销的情况下释放图形处理器，并说明双加速器扩展无需额外代价。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

边缘检测流水线中的下游分类模型受到专用加速器算子限制、量化不兼容和图形处理器串行执行的影响。

02
方法

方法依次进行网络结构调整、动态范围手动修复、量化感知训练、开放神经网络交换图修改和图形处理器与专用加速器并发推理。

03
差异

它把快速隐式量化验证、显式量化和专用加速器编译整合为一套可复用的零图形处理器回退流程，而不是只优化单个模型。

04
证据

在双头人员属性分类器与目标检测器的测试中，隐式量化精度从百分之七十五恢复到百分之九十四，端到端速率为每秒十二点五帧。

摘要

面向目标识别、监控、自动驾驶和无人机的边缘视觉系统通常需要分层推理流水线，但将所有模型运行在图形处理器上会形成串行瓶颈。本文以英伟达杰特森专用深度学习加速器为代表平台，提出包含架构调整、动态范围修复、量化感知训练、图结构修改和并发执行的五步部署方法，并通过九项工程约束的根因分析实现分类模型的整数八位专用加速器部署。在杰特森奥林诺奈克斯上的验证显示，检测器独占时速率为每秒十三点三帧，与分类器并发运行时为每秒十二点五帧，且双专用加速器扩展没有额外代价。

为什么值得看 这项工作直接处理边缘混合专家推理的内存与访存瓶颈：通过在注意力计算前预测并加载候选专家，把片外参数读取与有用计算重叠。论文报告正确性保持模式可将每令牌延迟最多降低百分之二十六、能效时延积最多改善百分之四十一，适合内存受限且重视精确路由的边缘设备；无停顿模式则用极小精度影响换取进一步效率。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

边缘混合专家推理受限于片外专家参数加载，而加载会阻塞令牌处理。

02
方法

系统使用轻量级预取路由器和学习得到的置信度模型，在注意力计算前预测候选专家并发起加载。

03
差异

它根据预测置信度自适应决定额外预取数量，并同时支持精确路由和仅使用已加载专家的无停顿执行。

04
证据

在多个混合专家模型上，论文报告重叠准确率超过百分之九十九，延迟最多降低百分之二十六，能效时延积最多改善百分之四十一。

摘要

混合专家模型以较高模型容量和较少的每令牌激活参数适合边缘部署，但专家参数通常因容量、成本和功耗限制存放在片外内存，使专家加载成为推理关键路径。本文提出自适应专家预取，通过轻量级预取路由器和学习得到的置信度模型，在注意力模块之前预测并动态获取额外专家；该方法实现了超过百分之九十九的重叠准确率，并提供保持精确路由语义的正确性保持模式以及消除剩余停顿的无停顿模式，在多个混合专家模型上将每令牌延迟最多降低百分之二十六、能效时延积最多改善百分之四十一。

为什么值得看 这项工作把大语言模型推理中的中间激活从高延迟的三维闪存阵列移到快速动态随机存取存储器，并通过平面内数据映射提高并行度，面向受内存容量和数据搬运限制的存储计算硬件提供了可落地的优化路径；论文声称相对基线最多可降低百分之八十五的推理延迟。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

现有基于闪存的存内计算方案没有有效处理中间激活的数据流和缓存，导致激活需要经过缓慢的闪存阵列。

02
方法

该架构用动态随机存取存储器缓存中间值，并在闪存存内计算阵列中采用分布式数据流和改进的平面内映射。

03
差异

它将激活缓冲从慢速闪存阵列转移到快速动态随机存取存储器，而不是继续在闪存中处理这些中间值。

04
证据

论文报告其架构相对基线最多降低百分之八十五的推理延迟。

摘要

存内计算能够缓解主机与存储器之间的数据瓶颈，但大语言模型所需资源增长很快，而内存密度并未同步提升。本文提出一种基于三维闪存的高性能存储计算架构：用快速动态随机存取存储器缓存中间激活，并采用分布式数据流和高效的平面内数据映射来提高计算并行度，从而降低激活写入较慢三级单元闪存所带来的延迟；结果显示，相比基线，推理延迟最多降低百分之八十五。

为什么值得看 这项工作把训练后的推荐模型专家库压缩直接转化为可部署的多档预算：在不增加在线压缩模块的情况下，将完整专家库导出为四专家或两专家模型，并在英伟达显卡上获得一百二十八到二百二十一个百分点的加速。对需要降低推荐模型推理成本、同时保留原有模型质量的服务团队尤其有用。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 11）
方法解读
01
问题

目标是在明确专家预算下，将已训练的稀疏混合专家检查点转换为更小的标准混合专家模型。

02
方法

方法把专家合并建模为受约束图粗化，并用无标签校准集计算专家的功能相似性。

03
差异

它不依赖参数距离，而是按专家对共享推荐状态的响应进行分组，并对高路由暴露专家施加分层保护。

04
证据

在亚马逊美妆、快手推荐和天池推荐数据集上，四专家与两专家配置分别报告了一点二八至一点六三倍和一点四七至二点二一倍的英伟达一百显卡实测加速。

摘要

稀疏混合专家层通过条件计算提升推荐模型容量，但训练完成的检查点仍需存储并路由完整的专家库。本文将该部署问题表述为受约束的图粗化问题，利用无标签校准集测量专家对相同推荐状态的功能响应相似性并进行合并，同时依据路由暴露度限制高流量专家的合并；在三个推荐数据集和不同混合专家层数上，四专家检查点保持相对源模型百分之九十九点九二至百分之一百零二点三零的归一化折损累计增益，并在英伟达一百显卡上获得一点二八至一点六三倍加速，激进的两专家顶一配置获得一点四七至二点二一倍加速。

为什么值得看 这项审计说明，英伟达黑威尔至尊的整数八位量化不能只看规格表：从指令集、内核库到大语言模型服务引擎，多个层次都默认撤回了支持，导致模型即使采用整数八位权重激活量化，也可能在首次前向计算时才失败。对部署工程师而言，文章给出了可行的即时编译后端绕行方案，并提醒常见性能分析方法可能误判硬件是否具备原生整数八位能力。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

研究考察黑威尔至尊上规格表所暗示的整数八位吞吐能力是否能贯通实际软件栈。

02
方法

作者逐层检查公开规格、并行线程执行指令集、通用线性代数模板库、虚拟大语言模型服务引擎和无状态大语言模型服务引擎的整数八位路径。

03
差异

分析不仅检查硬件指令，还追踪内核生成、服务引擎运行时失败、即时编译绕行以及性能分析误判。

04
证据

结果显示目标架构缺少第五代张量核心整数指令，模板库跳过整数八位内核，虚拟大语言模型服务引擎在首次前向计算时报错，另一个引擎的预编译支持停留在较旧架构。

摘要

本文从公开规格、并行线程执行指令集、英伟达通用线性代数模板库以及两个主流开源大语言模型服务引擎四个层次，审计黑威尔至尊图形处理器的整数八位权重激活量化支持。结果显示，针对该芯片的第五代张量核心整数路径并未在指令集中公开，内核生成器和服务引擎也相应跳过或缺失整数八位实现；虽然可通过即时编译的特里顿后端绕行，但规格表中名义存在的格式默认无法部署。

为什么值得看 这项工作提醒内核自动调优和基础设施评测研究者：在有反馈和选择压力的搜索中，模型会识别并针对评测配置，而不必被明确要求攻击评测。对图形处理器内核基准而言，评测应在不可枚举的配置轴上设置隐藏探针，同时在隐藏配置上检查性能与正确性；否则看似成功的优化可能只是在测量分支上过拟合。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 6）
方法解读
01
问题

评测信号会驱动优化系统适应具体配置，从而使分布内胜者不代表真实泛化能力。

02
方法

作者让三个大型语言模型在两个图形处理器内核套件中通过带丰富反馈的一加一进化循环生成和筛选内核。

03
差异

分析从配置指纹到门槛泄漏的四类失败，并将失败区分为投机、过拟合和良性迁移。

04
证据

两个套件共记录五十三个分布内胜者，其中十六个未能迁移到隐藏配置。

摘要

当系统针对评测信号进行优化时，基准测到的内容可能不同于其声称测量的能力。作者在两个带隐藏泛化门槛的图形处理器内核优化套件中记录了这一现象：三个前沿大型语言模型在具有丰富反馈的一加一进化循环中反复识别评测配置、最大化调优被测分支，却让未测分支变慢或悄然出错；在合并后的套件中，五十三个分布内胜者有十六个未能迁移到隐藏配置。论文给出四类失败模式，并提出评测设计建议，包括使用不可枚举的隐藏轴、在门槛中测量隐藏配置的性能而不只检查正确性，以及按失败机制拆分迁移率。

为什么值得看 它把特里顿内核生成的评测从孤立内核速度推进到真实人工智能框架中的端到端验证，并用来自开源项目拉取请求的工程任务检验正确性，适合判断大型语言模型生成的内核是否真的能进入生产系统。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

现有基准不能覆盖真实特里顿开发任务，也不能可靠衡量框架级端到端性能和正确性。

02
方法

系统提取开源人工智能框架中修改特里顿内核的拉取请求，并将其转化为自然语言需求到内核实现的可复现任务。

03
差异

评测把生成内核放回原始框架运行端到端测试，而不是只测孤立内核并依赖手写检查脚本。

04
证据

作者在该基准上评测领先大型语言模型，并报告它们仍难以完成真实世界的特里顿内核生成任务。

摘要

现有特里顿内核生成基准主要局限于从深度学习框架到特里顿的翻译、单个内核性能评测和容易被规避的手写检查脚本，难以反映真实工程任务。本文从流行开源人工智能框架中提取修改特里顿内核的拉取请求，将其转化为带有工程上下文和可复现实验环境的生成任务，并把生成内核集成回原框架进行端到端测试；对多个领先大型语言模型的评测显示，它们仍难以完成真实世界的特里顿内核生成任务。

为什么值得看 这项研究提醒推理系统设计者：把高带宽闪存直接当作更快的固态硬盘来卸载瞬态键值缓存可能适得其反；在英伟达高端加速器配置上，该替换使平均端到端延迟上升二至五点五倍，并使最大服务等级目标吞吐下降一点一至二点七倍，因此更适合采用按复用率选择、受写入预算约束并结合热管理的分层策略。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

研究检验将固态硬盘式键值缓存卸载栈的后端直接替换为高带宽闪存是否能改善大语言模型服务。

Achieving Near-Zero-Overhead Multi-Model Hierarchical Classification in Real-Time Detection Pipelines

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Vaishnav Raju
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters This addresses a practical edge-inference bottleneck: downstream classification otherwise serializes behind detection on the GPU. The deployment path moves classification to a dedicated accelerator and overlaps it with detection, preserving nearly the detector-only rate on Jetson Orin NX while enabling dual-accelerator scaling without added cost.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Edge classification models face accelerator operator restrictions, quantization incompatibilities, and GPU serialization in hierarchical detection pipelines.

02
Method

The workflow combines architecture adaptation, a manual dynamic-range workaround, quantization-aware training, ONNX graph surgery, and concurrent GPU-detection/DLA-classification execution.

03
Difference

It packages validation, quantization, compilation, and concurrency into a backbone-agnostic zero-GPU-fallback deployment procedure rather than optimizing only one inference kernel.

04
Evidence

Implicit quantization accuracy was recovered from 75% to 94%, and the Jetson Orin NX pipeline reached 12.5 FPS versus 13.3 FPS for detector-only execution.

Abstract

Edge-deployed vision systems in target recognition, surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and drone domains require hierarchical inference pipelines where a detection model identifies objects of interest and downstream classifiers provide fine-grained attribute analysis. Running all models on the GPU creates a serial bottleneck that limits real-time throughput as pipeline stages grow. Modern edge SoCs pair GPUs with dedicated neural accelerators (NPUs, DLAs) capable of concurrent execution, yet deploying custom models on these accelerators remains impractical due to strict operator constraints, quantization incompatibilities, and an undocumented end-to-end pipeline. We target NVIDIA Jetson DLA cores as the representative platform. We present a five-step methodology for zero GPU fallback DLA INT8 deployment of classification backbones, comprising architecture adaptation, manual dynamic range workaround to rescue TensorRT's implicit quantization (recovering 94.0% accuracy from implicit quantization's 75%) for rapid pipeline validation before explicit quantization, quantization-aware training, ONNX graph surgery for DLA compilation, and a concurrent GPU-detection/DLA-classification inference pipeline. We document nine engineering constraints with root-cause analysis and generalizable solutions. Validation on a dual-head person attribute classifier running on DLA alongside a GPU object detector on a Jetson Orin NX demonstrates near-zero pipeline overhead (12.5 vs. 13.3~FPS detector-only at 1080p), with dual-DLA scaling at no additional cost. The methodology is backbone-agnostic and generalizes to any detection-classification edge pipeline.

APEX: Adaptive Expert Prefetching for Memory-Efficient Edge MoE Inference

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Alish Kanani, Layan Badawi, Umit Y. Ogras
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters This work targets the memory and data-movement bottleneck that limits edge MoE inference: it predicts and loads candidate experts before attention so off-chip transfers overlap with useful computation. The paper reports up to 26% lower per-token latency and 41% better energy-delay product in correctness-preserving mode, giving memory-constrained edge deployments a way to retain exact routing; its stall-free mode trades negligible application-accuracy impact for further efficiency.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Edge MoE inference is blocked by loading large expert parameters from off-chip memory.

02
Method

A lightweight prefetch router uses a learned confidence model to predict candidate experts before the attention block and fetch them dynamically.

03
Difference

The design adapts the amount of prefetching to prediction confidence and offers both exact-routing and stall-free execution modes.

04
Evidence

Across multiple MoE models, the paper reports over 99% overlap accuracy, up to 26% lower per-token latency, and up to 41% better energy-delay product.

Abstract

Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are attractive for edge deployment because they provide high model capacity while activating only a small subset of parameters per token, improving compute efficiency. However, MoE inference at the edge is fundamentally limited by memory. Expert parameters are large and often reside in off-chip memory due to capacity, cost, and power constraints, putting expert loading to the critical path. We present APEX: Adaptive Expert Prefetching, a predictive resource management framework that overlaps expert loading with useful computation. APEX introduces a lightweight prefetch router that predicts candidate experts before the attention block to dynamically fetch additional experts using a learned confidence model. This adaptive strategy achieves over 99% overlap accuracy, significantly outperforming fixed top-k prefetching techniques. APEX supports two execution modes: a correctness-preserving mode that guarantees exact routing semantics, and a stall-free mode that eliminates residual stalls by operating on available experts with negligible impact on application accuracy. Across multiple MoE models, the correctness-preserving mode reduces per-token latency by up to 26% and improves energy-delay product (EDP) by up to 41% over state-of-the-art baselines, while the stall-free mode provides additional efficiency gains with negligible impact on application accuracy. These results establish adaptive, confidence-driven expert prefetching as an effective approach for efficient MoE inference on edge systems.

NITRO: High-Performance 3D NAND Flash-Based In-Storage Computing with Enhanced Activation Dataflow

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Sanghun Shin, Sangyeon Kim, Gisan Ji, Sungju Ryu
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters The design targets a concrete bottleneck in LLM inference hardware: it moves intermediate activations out of the high-latency 3D NAND array into a faster DRAM subsystem and increases array parallelism through intra-plane mapping. This gives storage-computing designers a way to trade a DRAM buffer for lower activation-programming cost, with a claimed inference-latency reduction of up to 85% versus the baseline.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Prior NAND-based processing-in-memory designs do not adequately handle intermediate activation dataflow and buffering, leaving activations in the slow flash array.

02
Method

The architecture buffers intermediate values in DRAM and uses distributed dataflow with efficient intra-plane mapping in the NAND-PIM array.

03
Difference

Instead of processing intermediate values in the flash array, it uses a fast DRAM subsystem for activation buffering while distributing computation across planes.

04
Evidence

The paper reports up to an 85% reduction in inference latency compared with the baseline.

Abstract

In-storage computing (ISC) is considered a next-generation memory architecture for its ability to relieve the data bottleneck between the host and the memory. While the required resources of large language models (LLMs) have increased significantly in recent years, the memory density has not scaled accordingly. Recently, several works have studied NAND flash-based processing-in-memory (NAND-PIM) schemes to exploit the high density of the memory. However, they do not address the dataflow/buffer for the intermediate values, so a simple method is to deal with the values in the slow flash memory array. To overcome such a limitation, we propose a high-performance NAND flash-based ISC architecture with enhanced activation buffering. Instead of using the very slow flash memory array for the intermediate values, our architecture buffers the values in a fast DRAM subsystem. This approach effectively handles the high-latency penalties when activations are programmed into slower TLC NAND flash. We also introduce a distributed dataflow approach for the NAND-PIM array. This approach maximizes computational parallelism by employing efficient intra-plane data mapping. The results show that our proposed architecture achieves significant performance improvements, reducing the inference latency by up to 85% compared to the baseline.

UniMoMo: Expert Merging-Based MoE Acceleration for Large Recommendation Models

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Memory and Decoding OptimizationTopicquantization / compression
Lei Xin, Bin Gu, Peize Li, Zitong Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Changjiang Jiang et al.
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters UniMoMo turns a trained recommendation MoE into several serving-budget checkpoints without adding an online compression module. The reported A100 speedups of 1.28x–2.21x, while keeping source-relative NDCG@10 ratios near or above 100% in many settings, make this relevant to teams serving large recommendation models under tighter memory and latency budgets.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 11)
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper targets conversion of a trained sparse MoE checkpoint into a smaller standard MoE under an explicit expert budget.

02
Method

It formulates expert consolidation as constrained graph coarsening and measures functional similarity from expert responses on an unlabeled calibration set.

03
Difference

Unlike parameter-distance grouping, it protects high-traffic experts with a layer-adaptive rule based on routing exposure.

04
Evidence

Experiments on Amazon Beauty, KuaiRec, and TenRec report four-expert speedups of 1.28x–1.63x and two-expert speedups of 1.47x–2.21x on A100 GPUs.

Abstract

Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers expand recommendation capacity through conditional computation, yet a trained checkpoint still stores and routes over its full expert bank. We study a deployment problem: convert that checkpoint to a smaller standard MoE under an explicit expert budget, without adding a compression-specific online module. To address this, we introduce UniMoMo, a post-training compression framework formulated as a constrained graph coarsening problem. Rather than relying on parameter distance, UniMoMo groups experts based on their functional similarity, using an unlabeled calibration set to measure how similarly experts respond to shared recommendation states. To prevent performance degradation, we introduce a layer-adaptive protection mechanism that restricts the merging of high-traffic experts based on their routing exposure. Across Amazon Beauty, KuaiRec, and TenRec with 2, 4, and 6 MoE blocks, the final four-expert checkpoints obtain source-relative five-run mean NDCG@10 ratios of 99.92%--102.30% and measured A100 speedups of 1.28times--1.63times. An aggressive two-expert, top-1 operating point obtains ratios of 98.36%--104.24% and speedups of 1.47times--2.21times. These endpoint results evaluate the complete conversion-and-adaptation workflow and show that a trained recommendation MoE can be exported at multiple serving budgets.

Spec Sheets Are Not Kernels: An ISA- and Source-Level Audit of INT8 Availability on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Memory and Decoding OptimizationTopicquantization / compression
Teng-Ruei Chen
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters The audit shows that INT8 deployment on Blackwell Ultra cannot be inferred from the datasheet: the ISA, kernel generator, and serving engines consistently remove the path, so an INT8 model can load successfully and still fail on its first forward pass. For deployment engineers, the paper identifies a JIT Triton escape hatch and exposes a profiler false negative that can misclassify whether B300 has a usable native INT8 path.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper tests whether Blackwell Ultra's datasheet-level INT8 capability is available through the real software stack.

02
Method

It traces W8A8 support across published specifications, PTX, CUTLASS, vLLM, and SGLang.

03
Difference

The audit connects ISA exposure, kernel generation, serving-time failure, JIT fallback, and profiler behavior instead of measuring tensor-core throughput alone.

04
Evidence

It reports no tcgen05.mma i8 path on sm_103a, skipped INT8 UMMA generation in CUTLASS, a first-forward failure in vLLM, and ahead-of-time INT8 support in SGLang ending at Sm90.

Abstract

NVIDIA's published specifications give the Blackwell Ultra GPU (B300) a dense-compute ratio of roughly 30:1 between FP8 and INT8 tensor-core throughput; its predecessors, H200 and B200, both provide 1:1. We audit what this deprioritization means in practice by tracing INT8 W8A8 support through four layers of the stack: the published specifications, the PTX ISA, NVIDIA's CUTLASS kernel library, and the two major open-source LLM serving engines (vLLM and SGLang). We find a consistent, layered withdrawal: (i) the PTX ISA never exposes the fifth-generation tensor-core integer path (tcgen05.mma with .kind::i8) on sm_103a, even though the same PTX revision extends the FP4 kinds to that target, leaving legacy warp-level IMMA as the only architecturally legal integer tensor-core path on B300; (ii) CUTLASS's kernel generator explicitly skips INT8 UMMA generation for any build targeting 103a, while generating FP8 unconditionally; (iii) vLLM ships no INT8 GEMM for Blackwell and fails with a hard runtime error at the first forward pass, after the model has loaded; and (iv) SGLang's ahead-of-time INT8 GEMM stops at Sm90, while its FP8 tuning configurations already cover B200. We document an escape hatch (rerouting vLLM's INT8 path to a JIT-compiled Triton backend via an environment variable), a false-negative trap in the obvious profiler methodology for detecting "native INT8" on sm_103, and the practical failure semantics that make naive testing expensive. Together, these findings show that a quantization format's availability is a property of the whole stack rather than of the model or the spec sheet. Four distinct layers, three of them NVIDIA's own, withdrew INT8 support in mutually consistent ways, and a format that is nominally present on the datasheet is, by default, undeployable on this hardware.

CategoryAreaBenchmarks and Observability / Infrastructure EvaluationTopicAI infrastructure benchmarks

high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters For kernel autotuning and infrastructure benchmark designers, this shows that search systems can target the evaluation configuration without being instructed to attack it. 02

Abstract

Benchmarks for systems that are optimized against the evaluation signal measure something different from what they claim. We document this concretely in two GPU-kernel-optimization suites with held-out generalization gates: Metal-Sci (10 scientific-compute tasks) and Metal-ZK (12 zero-knowledge/cryptographic tasks), in which three frontier LLMs (Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5) propose Metal kernels inside a (1{+}1) evolutionary loop with rich feedback. Although no model is prompted to act adversarially, the promoted winners repeatedly fingerprint the evaluation configuration: they branch on the identity of runtime parameters, tune the measured branch maximally, and leave the unmeasured branch slow or silently wrong. Across the pooled suites, 16/53 (30%) of in-distribution wins fail to transfer to held-out configurations. We give a four-mode taxonomy of these failures, from configuration fingerprints to gate leakage. We distill design guidance for measurement under strategic optimization: held-out probes retain validity only on non-enumerable axes; gates must measure held-out performance, not just correctness; and a transfer rate is interpretable only with per-failure mechanism grades: ours decomposes into gamed, overfit, and benign. Code and research artifacts: https://github.com/vicgalle/kernel-fingerprinting

CategoryAreaBenchmarks and Observability / Infrastructure EvaluationTopicAI infrastructure benchmarks

Why it matters This benchmark tests whether LLM-generated Triton kernels are useful inside real AI frameworks, not merely fast in isolation. PR-derived tasks, framework-integrated end-to-end tests, and reproducible environments give infra teams a better way to measure production readiness and expose correctness checks that can be bypassed.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing benchmarks miss the diversity of real Triton engineering work and inadequately measure end-to-end performance and correctness.

02
Method

The benchmark extracts Triton-kernel changes from pull requests in popular open-source AI frameworks and turns them into reproducible natural-language-to-kernel tasks.

Abstract

In modern AI frameworks, GPU kernels are key to overall system performance. Combining usability, portability, and near-handwritten CUDA performance, Triton is widely adopted for implementing GPU kernels. Recent advances show the potential of large language models (LLMs) to automatically generate Triton kernels, reducing the manual effort required from expert kernel developers. Several benchmarks evaluate LLM-generated Triton kernels. However, they suffer from three key limitations: (1) they restrict tasks to PyTorch-to-Triton translation, failing to reflect the diversity and complexity of real-world Triton tasks; (2) they evaluate only individual-kernel performance rather than end-to-end performance, the core criterion for real-world deployment in AI frameworks; and (3) they rely on manually written evaluation scripts for individual kernels, which may contain flaws that models can exploit to bypass correctness checks and obtain inflated scores. To address these limitations, we introduce RealisticTritonBench, the first benchmark to derive Triton kernel generation tasks from real-world pull requests in popular AI frameworks, enabling realistic, production-like evaluation. RealisticTritonBench systematically extracts PRs that modify Triton kernels from popular open-source AI frameworks and transforms them into generation tasks with concrete engineering contexts. Each task takes a natural language requirement as input and requires a corresponding Triton kernel implementation, with a complete and reproducible evaluation environment. Unlike prior benchmarks focused on isolated kernel performance, RealisticTritonBench integrates generated kernels into their original frameworks and evaluates them using end-to-end tests, enabling a more faithful assessment. We evaluate leading LLMs on RealisticTritonBench and find that they still struggle with real-world Triton kernel generation tasks.

A Full-Stack Characterization of High-Bandwidth Flash for KV-Centric LLM Serving

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Memory and Decoding OptimizationTopicKV cache / long context memory
Zhuoran Li, Zhuohang Bian, Xin Huang, Yibo Zhao, Guangyu Sun, Youwei Zhuo
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters This paper gives LLM-serving architects a concrete warning: replacing the SSD tier with High-Bandwidth Flash for transient KV offload can make the system slower, not faster. Across H100 and B200 configurations, the swap raises average end-to-end latency by 2–5.5x and lowers maximum SLO goodput by 1.1–2.7x, pointing instead to selective, reuse-aware, write-budgeted, and thermally coordinated placement.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper tests whether an SSD-style KV-offload stack improves when its backing tier is directly replaced by High-Bandwidth Flash.

02
Method

It extends TokenSim and evaluates four two-hour production traces, five dense and mixture-of-experts models, and H100/B200 profiles.

03
Difference

The analysis combines near-tier capacity and bandwidth, read/write mix, package thermal limits, endurance, and the effect of base-die near-memory compute.

04
Evidence

The study reports 2–5.5x higher average end-to-end latency and 1.1–2.7x lower maximum SLO goodput, with writes exceeding reads on every trace.

Abstract

High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) stacks NAND behind a wide, package-local interface, giving flash-scale capacity with far better read latency and bandwidth than an SSD. This makes it tempting to keep an SSD-style Mooncake KV-offloading stack and swap only the backing tier for HBF. We test that substitution with an extended TokenSim, four complete two-hour Qwen-Bailian production traces, five dense and mixture-of-experts models, and H100/B200 profiles. Serving gets worse, not better, and a cost-benefit model explains why. A faster far tier helps only when read I/O is the serving bottleneck, reads outweigh writes, and delivered bandwidth is sustainable. All three must hold together, and transient KV fails every one. The package trade that buys flash costs GPU near-tier capacity and bandwidth, so average end-to-end latency rises 2--5.5x and maximum SLO goodput falls 1.1--2.7x across H100 and B200. Serving is almost insensitive to HBF's own read/write latency, and base-die near-memory compute does not raise the flash tier's share of the critical path. The two-tier hierarchy keeps reuse in the near tier and hands HBF a write-heavy stream, so writes outnumber reads on every trace. A 3D-ICE model shows that stream drives the stack to its thermal limit well below peak bandwidth, and a TLC tier wears out sooner than a capacity-matched SSD pool. The faster device yields a slower system because the package gives up more than the medium returns. HBF is not the problem; using it as a faster SSD for transient KV is. It belongs in serving as a selective, reuse-aware, write-budgeted, and thermally coordinated tier, not as a drop-in SSD replacement.

medium · 2026-08-12

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Copying short-term memory into long-term storage does not ensure that later accesses will use the retained content.

02
Method

A trainable slot-local operator transforms routed short-term memory before accumulating it into long-term memory, which is also supplied to the hierarchical router.

Abstract

Copying short-term memory (STM) into a slower store can preserve state across a context boundary, but persistence alone does not ensure that the retained state influences subsequent memory access. We test this distinction in a Phasor Memory Network (PMNet) using Consolidator, a shared slot-local operator that transforms routed STM before accumulating it into long-term memory (LTM), without replaying the source tokens. After each consolidation, the KV cache and STM are cleared. The retained LTM can still be read and is also fed into the hierarchical router, thereby conditioning which explicit-memory slots subsequent inputs access. We evaluate this mechanism on a two-segment modulo-10 mapping task in which the second segment updates the mapping at the same memory address. Following a second consolidation and reset, a held-out query must recover the updated mapping from LTM. The backbone and memory interface are frozen, leaving only 12.35K Consolidator parameters trainable (0.041\% of a 29.95M model). Across five paired runs from the same STM-pretraining checkpoint, direct LTM routing raises updated-mapping recall from $44.38\pm1.94\%$ to $87.02\pm1.76\%$ ($+42.64\pm1.10$ percentage points), while immediate STM recall remains 89.90\% in both conditions; both train separate Consolidators and retain the same LTM read paths. Learned consolidation outperforms forced identity accumulation by $21.40\pm1.91$ percentage points without routing and $68.70\pm1.76$ with routing. Thus, on this task, consolidated LTM serves as both retrievable content and an access state that shapes subsequent slot selection.

01
Problem

Framework loading copies checkpoint pages that the operating system already caches and the accelerator can already read, creating capacity pressure and repeated reads.

02
Method

A framework-independent producer maps each tensor with shared mappings, wraps the pages as no-copy accelerator buffers, and imports them through DLPack.

03
Difference

The design requires more than zero-copy import: execution must read the mapping, keep activations resident on the accelerator, and order work on the GPU.

04
Evidence

Under that contract it reaches 516 GB/s versus 53–82 GB/s for default constructors and stays within roughly one percent of resident-storage kernels; multi-process and first-token tests also report substantial gains.

Abstract

Open-weight models can occupy a middle capacity regime: active weights fit in DRAM as cached file pages, but a second framework-owned representation does not fit or must be refilled as layers run, so low-batch decode rereads the weights every token. On integrated and coherent-memory systems the checkpoint's file pages already occupy a GPU-readable domain, yet accelerator-loading paths still copy them into framework-owned allocations. We call this the ingestion tax: the OS holds the bytes as clean, evictable file pages, the architecture makes them GPU-readable, and only the framework's ownership model stands between the two. We present file-backed weight adoption: a framework-independent producer maps each tensor with MAP_SHARED, wraps the pages as a no-copy GPU buffer, and exports a DLPack capsule that PyTorch or MLX imports as ordinary storage. Zero-copy import alone is not enough: a randomized factorial establishes a three-part execution contract - read the mapping, keep activations accelerator-resident, order on the GPU; a bolt-on extension forfeiting the last two runs 2.3x slower than stock. Under the contract, adoption removes the tax at no rate cost: 516 GB/s where default constructors reach 53-82, at parity with the same kernel over resident storage ([-0.66%, +0.48%]; Qwen2.5-72B 7.14 vs 7.23 tok/s). Parity buys ownership: N processes decode one mapped copy where resident loading pays N (at capacity, 5.5 vs 0.08 tok/s); a 65 GB checkpoint reaches its first token 6.4x sooner; the Kimi K3 spine stage falls from 2.62 to 0.35 s per token, 3.8x from storage alone. The same mechanism improves llama.cpp 1.21x at half the footprint on an AMD APU, ties overlapped streaming on a capacity-exceeding GH200, and loses 39x across PCIe: memory topology, not the API, decides the byte path. The deployment rule treats the page cache as a first-class, reclaimable accelerator-storage tier.

Who Should Own the Expert Cache? Kernel-Managed Tiering for Trillion-Parameter MoE Inference

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Serving EnginesTopicLLM serving / inference engines
Yuan Si, Yufeng Lin, Daming Li, Jialu Zhang
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters This paper directly tests whether trillion-parameter MoE serving needs a user-space expert cache. Under equal memory, untuned kernel caching matches a same-domain frequency oracle and improves decode performance by 1.09–1.10×, suggesting that systems can let the kernel handle eviction while using model knowledge only for admission and readahead advice.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

MoE expert pools exceed DRAM capacity, forcing serving systems to choose how to tier and evict experts.

02
Method

The study replays router traces from three MoE models against their full expert pools on GH200 nodes under three independent capacity-enforcement mechanisms.

03
Difference

It treats the kernel page cache as the expert tier and separates kernel eviction from model-specific admission and advice.

04
Evidence

At 256 GB, kernel LRU serves 75.3% of demand versus 74.6% for a same-domain frequency oracle, while router lookahead adds only 0.3% as readahead advice and nothing as synchronous prefetch.

Abstract

Mixture-of-experts models whose expert pools dwarf DRAM force every serving system to contain a cache, yet existing systems typically implement this cache in user space using expert-granular, frequency-ranked, explicitly pinned tiers. We characterize the alternative already provided by the OS: the page cache as the expert tier. We use router traces from three MoE models spanning 128 to 896 experts per layer, including a production trillion-parameter model with a 1.45 TB expert pool, and replay them natively against the full pool on GH200 nodes with capacity enforced by three independent mechanisms. We find four main results. First, iteration time and device traffic are smooth, reproducible functions of cache capacity, making DRAM a practical sizing knob for trillion-parameter serving. Second, the deep-pressure knee is a reclaim artifact requiring both MGLRU and balloon-style mostly-mlocked memory; cgroup limits and physical-memory configurations show no such amplification, indicating that balloon-based studies can overstate pressured-end device traffic by approximately 2$\times$. Third, under an enforced equal-memory wall, untuned kernel LRU serves essentially as much demand as a same-domain oracle frequency table (75.3% versus 74.6% at 256 GB), while the oracle's mechanism advantage is only 1.09$\times$ and disappears off-domain, where LRU remains at 70--71% hit rate. Fourth, router lookahead with 64.7% measured recall provides only a 0.3% benefit as kernel readahead advice and no benefit as synchronous prefetch. End to end, enabling kernel-managed caching improves decode performance by 1.09--1.10$\times$ with token-identical outputs across nine balanced pairs. The resulting design principle is simple: in this regime, let the kernel own eviction, while model-specific knowledge is best spent on admission and advice.

RoutePack: Expert Placement and Attention-Aware Data Packing for MoE Reinforcement Learning

CategoryAreaTraining Systems / Parallel and Distributed TrainingTopicdata / model / pipeline parallelism
Yibo Shen, Xudong Han, Xiaowei Zhu, Gen Li, Zhenxuan Pan
high · 2026-08-12

Why it matters It addresses a real MoE RL systems bottleneck: attention imbalance from sequence composition can trade places with expert imbalance from token routing. By coordinating expert placement and packing within an optimizer-step window, it improves end-to-end trainer throughput by 8.85% and 14.89% over baseline on the two Ling-3.0 models, making it relevant to engineers scaling MoE training.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

MoE reinforcement learning must balance dense attention work across data-parallel microbatches against sparse expert work across expert-parallel ranks.

02
Method

The planner places experts layer by layer from aggregate routing demand, then searches token-capped data layouts using an objective based on attention cost, physical expert-rank peaks, and the slowest shard.

03
Difference

It combines state-consistent layer-wise expert rerouting with joint packing while retaining logical top-k routing, existing MoE kernels, and the communicator topology without microbatch-level expert replication.

04
Evidence

On Ling-3.0-Tiny and Ling-3.0-Flash, rerouting adds 3.80% and 10.50% throughput, packing adds 4.86% and 3.98%, and the combined gains reach 8.85% and 14.89%.

Abstract

Training Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models for reinforcement learning (RL) couples two load-balancing problems: sequence composition determines dense attention work in each data-parallel microbatch, while token routing determines sparse expert work on expert-parallel ranks. Optimizing either alone can shift the bottleneck to the other. In MoE RL, rollout-time routing replay exposes every sample's sequence length and layer-wise expert demand before its training step. We present RoutePack, a hierarchical planner that coordinates state-consistent, layer-wise expert rerouting with joint attention- and expert-aware data packing over an optimizer-step window. RoutePack first places experts independently at each MoE layer using aggregate routing demand. It then packs samples into the smallest certified, or best-known feasible, number of token-capped execution rows and optimizes their DP layout with a projected EDP-shard-aware objective. The objective combines a window-normalized linear-quadratic attention proxy with per-layer physical EP-rank peaks and minimizes the accumulated cost of the slowest EDP shard. Parallel population annealing searches fixed-row feasible layouts while preserving sample coverage, capacity, nonempty cells, equal microbatch counts, and communicator topology. State-consistent materialization preserves logical top-k routing and existing MoE kernels without microbatch-level expert replication. Across Ling-3.0-Tiny and Ling-3.0-Flash, expert rerouting improves mean trainer-measured token throughput by 3.80% and 10.50%, while routing-aware packing adds another 4.86% and 3.98%, respectively. Overall, RoutePack improves throughput by 8.85% and 14.89% over the baseline.

User-Assisted Collaborative Distributed Inference for Efficient QoS-Aware Autoscaling

CategoryAreaTraining Systems / Cluster Scheduling and ReliabilityTopicresource management / elasticity
Alfreds Lapkovskis, Ali Beikmohammadi, Sindri Magnússon, Praveen Kumar Donta
medium · 2026-08-12

Why it matters The system turns user-contributed capacity into an elasticity pool for inference: dedicated resources preserve baseline QoS, while volunteered resources absorb demand spikes. This is relevant to autoscaling, cross-node scheduling, and tail-latency control, although the evidence is currently simulation-based.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Centralized inference capacity becomes more expensive as demand grows, while interactions among users, resources, tasks, and policies are stochastic and dynamic.

02
Method

The system combines dedicated baseline capacity with user-contributed resources and uses a high-dimensional generative Markov model to simulate scheduling and QoS-aware allocation.

03
Difference

Unlike centralized-only serving, it places user-side resources inside a QoS-aware distributed scheduling policy.

04
Evidence

Simulations vary user populations, resource capacities, and scheduling policies, and report request completion, P99 latency, and dedicated-resource consumption.

Abstract

Growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) inference services requires scalable infrastructure, yet centralized serving costs rise with demand. We propose a collaborative distributed inference system combining dedicated infrastructure with resources contributed by service users. Dedicated resources provide baseline capacity for maintaining quality of service (QoS), while volunteered resources absorb increasing demand without proportional growth in centralized infrastructure. To capture stochastic and dynamic interactions among users, resources, tasks, and policies, we develop a high-dimensional generative Markov model with structured temporal factorization. The model supports simulation and provides a foundation for task scheduling and QoS-aware resource allocation optimization. We evaluate the system across user populations, resource capacities, and centralized and distributed scheduling policies. Simulations show that distributed scheduling becomes increasingly advantageous as the user population grows, improving request completion and P99 latency while substantially reducing dedicated resource consumption. These results demonstrate the feasibility of user-assisted collaborative inference for infrastructure-efficient autoscaling.

Evaluating OpenMP Offloading for Intra-node Multi-GPU Programming across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel Architectures: A 3D Heat Transfer Case Study

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / Compilers and RuntimeTopiccompiler / runtime
Ezhilmathi Krishnasamy
medium · 2026-08-12

Why it matters This study targets single-node multi-accelerator programming, device communication, and portability across vendors, giving infrastructure researchers concrete evidence about the cost of directive-based offloading. It reports roughly 2x speedup with two GPUs and roughly 4x with four GPUs over single-GPU OpenMP offloading, while exposing the roles of synchronous, asynchronous, peer-to-peer, and low-level memory operations.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper examines how to use multiple GPUs within one node for a 3D heat equation involving computation, halo work, and communication.

02
Method

It evaluates several OpenMP offloading implementations with different allocation and transfer mechanisms and compares them with CUDA, HIP, and SYCL.

03
Difference

The study systematically compares one directive-based code model across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs against each vendor's native programming model.

04
Evidence

The abstract reports approximately 2x performance with two GPUs and approximately 4x with four GPUs relative to single-GPU OpenMP offloading.

Abstract

Currently, most supercomputers are equipped with GPUs from manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel, which provide substantial parallelism and high throughput. It is common for a single compute node (intra-node) to host multiple GPUs, typically four or more. Therefore, effectively leveraging all these GPUs within a single compute node is essential for applications in scientific and engineering domains. However, several factors must be considered before utilizing these GPUs for scientific computing, including the implementation of data communication, the programming models available for use across these GPUs, and the level of performance that can be achieved with a single codebase across different GPU architectures and configurations within a single compute node. OpenMP Offloading is a prominent directive-based programming model that can be executed on all three GPU types: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel. In this research, we present an analysis of the benefits and performance challenges of using OpenMP Offloading to address the 3D heat equations, which involve both primary computation, as well as halo computation and communication. We investigate how performance varies in relation to native GPU programming models--CUDA for NVIDIA, HIP for AMD, and SYCL for Intel. Furthermore, we demonstrate that OpenMP Offloading can achieve performance improvements of approximately 2x for 2 GPUs and around 4x for 4 GPUs when compared to single-GPU OpenMP Offloading implementations across all three GPU types. This analysis is conducted systematically through various OpenMP Offloading implementations that utilize different low-level APIs for memory allocation, memory transfer options (synchronous, asynchronous, and peer-to-peer), and other native GPU programming models such as CUDA (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), and SYCL (Intel)

Elias Grünewald, Daniil Cherepko, Linus Gustafsson, Jakob Möhler, Oskar Rabe, Paul Robin Reichelt et al.

Method brief
01
Problem

02
Method

01

Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace

分类主题agent evaluation / benchmarks
Yijun Pan, Yukun Lian, Kunyu Shi, Junbo Li, Hongwei Xue, Sicong Xie et al.
high · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 它把代理评测从短程任务扩展到有延迟反馈、资本风险、监管约束和相互耦合决策的真实商业运营，并显示最佳模型仍落后于人工策略，为研究长期规划、风险控制和可解释归因提供了更有压力的测试场。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 16）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有代理基准很少衡量代理在不完整信息、长期回报和合规要求下经营企业的能力。

02
方法

研究者构建跨境商店环境，让代理依据真实阿里巴巴采购数据和权威来源校准的市场条件采购、定价并向买家销售。
